Early versions of Write only work with Write (.wri) files, but after Windows 3.0, Write became capable of reading and composing early Word (.doc) documents. With Windows 3.1, Write became OLE capable. In Windows 95, Write was replaced with WordPad.

records.name: XBIN (eXtended BIN)
records.summary: XBIN (eXtended BIN) is a character graphics format, widely used for ANSI art. It was designed to be a successor to BIN format [fmt/208] and uses a specialized run-length encoding (RLE) compression algorithm. Although XBIN is considered to be a graphics format, it is not required to have an image. The format can be used for storing pre-made fonts and pre-made palettes which can be loaded from a viewer/editor. It is closely tied to the capabilities of the text modes of VGA graphics cards. The font can be customized, though limited to 16 colours only. XBIN allows for binary images up to 65536 columns wide, and 65536 lines high, with an alternate set of palette colours either in blink or non-blink mode. It also allows for different textmode fonts from 1 to 32 scanlines high, consisting of either 256 or 512 different characters, and its file size is smaller by using more efficient compression system to its predecessor BIN format [fmt/208].

records.name: XIMG (Extended GEM Bit Image)
records.summary: The XIMG (Extended GEM Bit Image) image format is more developed version of GEM raster Image [x-fmt/159] which allows for standardised verison of storing colour palettes. It originated due to the specification of GEM format being ambiguous as to the format of color images. The GEM raster format (also known as GEM VDI Bit Image; GEM Bit Image; GEM Image; GEM Bitmap; or IMG) is an image format native to the Graphical Environment Manager (GEM) operating system and developed at Digital Research. The format was used by GEM Paint and Ventura Publisher, and by a variety of Atari ST software.

records.name: XL-Paint
records.summary: XL-Paint is a graphic format used for storing images created by XL-Paint program, a program used for the Atari 8-bit family of computers, introduced in 1979. It uses .raw file extension, files begin with ASCII "XLPB" and are either 792 or 15372 bytes long. The Atari 8-bit family is a series of 8-bit home computers introduced by Atari, Inc. All machines are based on the MOS Technology 6502 CPU running at 1.79 MHz, and were the first home computers designed with custom coprocessor chips.

records.name: XML Property List
records.summary: In the OS X, iOS, NeXTSTEP, and GNUstep programming frameworks, property list files store serialized objects. It is the standard way to save and load data between the internal representation within the objects defined in an Objective-C program and disk files, in order to store program settings and other data. This is the XML version but there is also a binary version of the format.

records.name: XML Schema Definition
records.summary: XML Schemas Definition files define the structure, and content of XML documents. They are used to express a set of rules to which an XML document must conform in order to be considered 'valid' in accordance to the particular schema referenced. Full specifications can be found at http://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-0/

records.name: XML Shareable Playlist Format
records.summary: Xspf is a format for sharing playlists, supported by many applications. It uses xml, so is easily edited with a text editor. The official website gives useful information as to the structure of xspf files: https://www.xspf.org/quickstart

records.name: XV Thumbnail
records.summary: XV Thumbnail, also known as XV Visual Schnauzer format, is an image file format used by the XV image viewer for its thumbnail cache. Such files may retain the original extension or may have .p7 appended.

records.name: XYWrite for Windows Document
records.summary: Microsoft Write is a basic word processor included with Windows 1.0 and later, until Windows NT 3.5. Throughout its lifespan it was minimally updated, and is comparable to early versions of MacWrite. Early versions of Write only work with Write (.wri) files, but after Windows 3.0, Write became capable of reading and composing early Word (.doc) documents. With Windows 3.1, Write became OLE capable. In Windows 95, Write was replaced with WordPad.

records.name: XZ File Format
records.summary: The XZ file format is intended as a single-file compression format, similar in utility to Gzip.

records.name: Yamaha PSR Disk Manager File
records.summary: Files developed by Yamaha, created on floppy disks used with Yamaha PSR keyboards. The files contain the information the keyboard uses to access the other files on the disk. Mng files do not contain any voice or style data.

records.name: Yamaha TX Wave Audio
records.summary: The Yamaha TX Wave Audio format is 12-bit audio wave file created by the Yamaha TX16W sampler. The Yamaha TX16W is a rack-mount sampler sound module with up to 50 kHz mono and 33 kHz stereo sampling. The format is proprietary created by Yamaha, similar to a .WAV file and supports 16, 33, and 50 kHz samples. The file consists of a 32 byte header followed by the actual waveform. This file fomat has multiple extensions, some of which have yet not been identified. The Yamaha SY Series Wave files also can use the same file extension and a simililar BOF sequence of 0x4C4D38393533. Please use links provided to view the full format specification.

records.name: Yamaha Wave Audio
records.summary: Yamaha Wave Audio signature describes formats relevant to Yamaha Wave files, these formats are proprietary and created by Yamaha. There are several versions of these file formats with a numerous examples of extensions. This entry describes generic Yamaha wave format, and PRONOM holds a separate entry on Yamaha TX Wave Audio. Please contact the PRONOM team if you have more information regarding Yamaha Wave formats.

records.name: YAML
records.summary: YAML is data serialisation format which uses a text file organised in a human-readable form. YAML can be used with several platforms of programming languages such as C, Perl, PHP, Python, Ruby, Javascript and others.

records.name: YAODL (Yet Another Object Description Language) File

magic.notes: YAODL (Yet Another Object Description Language) File

records.summary: SGI YAODL (Yet Another Object Description Language) is a description language used for storing 3D object data to disk files. YAODL is an obsolete format created specifically for the Silicon Graphics Powerflip demo program, but it is not widely supported by SGI. The format is an example of a basic vector-object description language and is stored in plain text (ASCII) format.

records.name: yEnc Encoded File
records.summary: yEnc is a binary-to-text encoding mechanism initially developed by Jürgen Helbing for transferring binary files in messages, such as via Usenet or email.

records.name: Z Compressed Data
records.summary: Z Compressed Data are files that have been compressed by Unix's shell compression program, compress. The compress software was developed by Spencer Thomas in 1984 and uses LZW algorithm. The format has lossless data, it can be compressed and decompressed using the Unix and Linux operating systems.

records.name: Z Print Build File
records.summary: Files used by Z Print or 3D Print that run 3D CJP Printers or former Z Corp Printers. They were used by Z corp 310s, 510s, 810s, 400s, 150s, 250s, 350s, 450s, 650s, 850s or 3D Systems 160s, 260s, 360s, 460s, 660s, 860s, or 4500s.

records.name: ZBrush MatCap
records.summary: ZBrush Material format is used with 3-D materials by the ZBrush software. It is used with the MatCap (Material Capture) tool that uses calibration markers to capture information from photographs and other images. Each of these markers samples a single point on the image and defines the colour, texture and lightining of the surface to build up a material map that simulates the lighting and material properties from the photograph. The HDRP replaces all of the materials and lighting in the scene with what is in the MatCap.

records.name: ZFO (Form) File
records.summary: ZFO file is a ZIP archive file containing the FO electronic form. The FO electronic form is a XML data file containing an electronic form intended for usage in the 602XML applications. The form is a composure of the layout structure using XSL-FO, data instance and data model using generic XML elements defined in the 602XML framework. The whole electronic form structure is always embedded into a digital signature represented by XML elements of the XML Signature standard. ZFO file can be password protected.

records.name: ZFO (Message) File
records.summary: This variant of ZFO file is container for delivered data mailbox messages provided by Česká pošta, s.p. ZFO file is a ZIP archive file (PKCS #7 Cryptographic Message File) composing of the layout structure using XML elements (envelope) and data instance encoded as Base64 (message content). The message may contain one or more attachments in the file format specified in Annex 3 to Decree No. 194/2009 Col. The whole structure is always embedded into a digital signature represented by XML elements of the XML Signature standard.

records.name: ZFO (Proof of Delivery) File
records.summary: This variant of ZFO file is container for proof of delivery of data mailbox messages provided by Česká pošta, s.p. in three versions: 1. proof of delivery; 2. confirmation of delivery; 3. delivery failure. ZFO file is a ZIP archive file (PKCS #7 Cryptographic Message File) composing of the layout structure using XML elements. The whole structure is always embedded into a digital signature represented by XML elements of the XML Signature standard.

records.name: ZFO (Sent Message) File
records.summary: This variant of ZFO file is container for sent data mailbox messages provided by Česká pošta, s.p. ZFO file is a ZIP archive file (PKCS #7 Cryptographic Message File) composing of the layout structure using XML elements (envelope) and data instance encoded as Base64 (message content). The message may contain one or more attachments in the file format specified in Annex 3 to Decree No. 194/2009 Col. The whole tructure is always embedded into a digital signature represented by XML elements of the XML Signature standard.

records.name: ZIP Format
records.summary: A popular archive format supported by most modern operating systems. It can contain one or more files and can utilize any of a number of compression methods.

records.name: ZISRAW (CZI) File Format
records.summary: The CZI file format was developed by ZEISS for use in microscopy imaging. It contains the image data plus metadata about the capture, such as image information and capture settings.

records.name: ZModeler Z3D
records.summary: Z3D is the native format of the ZModeler 3D modelling application.

records.name: Zoner Callisto Metafile
records.summary: Callisto is a vector graphics editor created by Czech company Zoner Software. This version of the .zmf format is based on Microsoft's OLE2 Compound Document File Format.

records.name: Zoom Project Settings
records.summary: File made by the Zoom H5, a portable audio recorder which is in widespread use. The hprj file is outputted by the device, sitting alongside the audio files. The file holds metadata information including project title, recording date etc. The H5 records in 2GB chunks, and when that is exceeded splits the recording into smaller chunks. The metadata tells the H5 which files go together and their order.

records.name: Zoom Project Settings
records.summary: File made by the Zoom H6, a portable audio recorder which is in widespread use. The hprj file is outputted by the device, sitting alongside the audio files. The file holds metadata information including project title, recording date etc. The H5 records in 2GB chunks, and when that is exceeded splits the recording into smaller chunks. The metadata tells the H6 which files go together and their order.

records.name: ZoomBrowser Ex Thumbnail Cache
records.summary: ZoomBrowser Ex Thumbnail Cache (ZbThumbnail.info) is a file created by Canon's ZoomBrowser Ex image organizing application, likely used to display thumbnail images within the application.

records.name: Zoomify Image Format
records.summary: Zoomify offers the ability to pinto high resolution images. It works by converting a high resolution image into a collection of JPEG tiles that are stored within a .zif file. This file can in turn be displayed within a web browser with the aid of a javascript library.

records.name: Zope Export File
records.summary: Zope is an open source web application server. The export mechanism allows Zope objects to be exported from one instance to another.

records.name: ZPAQ Archive Format
records.summary: ZPAQ is an open source command line file archiver developed by Matt Mahoney.

records.name: ZyXEL Voice Format Audio
records.summary: ZyXEL Voice Audio files were originally developed by Zyxel Communications for the Zyxel Z-Fax modem software application. These files are capable of digitizing speech to transfer data through software such as Z-Fax or VoiceConnect, using compression betweeen 19.2k CPS(ADPCM) and 9.6k CPS (CELP).
